articles.title: Frank Gansz Jr. cause of death: What we know about the longtime NFL coach’s death at the age of 64
articles.standfirst: Gansz Jr. coached the Raiders, Chiefs and Ravens during a nine-season NFL career
articles.summary: Gansz Jr. coached the Raiders, Chiefs and Ravens during a nine-season NFL career
articles.body:
Frank Gansz Jr., a longtime special teams coach who worked in the NFL and several professional football leagues, has died at 64.

His death was confirmed by the United Football League and the St. Louis Battlehawks, his most recent team. However, his cause of death hasn’t been publicly disclosed.

Gansz Jr. is believed to have died over the weekend, with tributes quickly emerging from across the football community.

“The United Football League and St. Louis Battlehawks extend their deepest condolences to the Gansz family, his friends, former players and coaches, and the countless people throughout the football community whose lives he touched during his remarkable coaching career,” read a statement by the United Football League.

His death also marks the loss of a prominent member of one of football’s most respected special teams families. His father, Frank Gansz Sr. , was an influential special teams coach who spent decades in professional football and played a major role in establishing the special teams coordinator position as a specialized coaching role.

Frank Gansz Sr. also served as head coach of the Kansas City Chiefs in 1987 and 1988 and later earned a Super Bowl ring with the St. Louis Rams. He was part of the Rams’ “Greatest Show on Turf” team that defeated the Tennessee Titans in Super Bowl XXXIV following the 1999 season.

Frank Gansz Jr.’s coaching career

Gansz Jr. carved out an impressive coaching career of his own, spending nine seasons in the NFL. His professional journey included stops with the Oakland Raiders, Kansas City Chiefs and Baltimore Ravens.

His longest NFL tenure came with Kansas City, where he worked as special teams coach from 2001 through 2005. During that period, he helped oversee one of the league’s standout special teams units, with explosive return specialist Dante Hall emerging as one of its biggest stars.

Hall became known as “The Human Joystick” because of his ability to change games with his speed and elusiveness on returns. His performances helped make Kansas City’s special teams a major weapon during the early 2000s.

Gansz Jr. began his coaching career in the college ranks before reaching the NFL. He spent five seasons at the University of Houston from 1993 to 1997, working with tight ends and special teams. He later coached at programs including UCLA, SMU, West Point, Kansas and Pittsburgh.

At UCLA, Gansz Jr. was involved in the development of kicker Kai Forbath, who went on to become an accomplished NFL kicker. He later returned to SMU, where his father had previously coached.

After leaving the college ranks, Gansz Jr. continued working in professional football, taking coaching roles in leagues including the CFL, XFL and USFL before joining the UFL’s St. Louis Battlehawks.

While the circumstances surrounding his death remain private and no cause has been announced, the response from the football world has underscored Gansz Jr.’s influence.

articles.title: Top option for 33rd NFL team backed by All-Pro QB as Roger Goodell suggests expansion franchise in foreign country
articles.standfirst: While a new NFL franchise entering the fray is far from coming to fruition, the league clearly wants to keep building internationally.
articles.summary: While a new NFL franchise entering the fray is far from coming to fruition, the league clearly wants to keep building internationally.
articles.body:
Over the past few days, the idea of an NFL expansion team joining the league has once again heated up. This time around, the discussion is different, as it's centered around the potential of a new franchise outside of the United States.

This was all kickstarted by NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell , who made a surprising comment in regards to the possibility of an international NFL franchise: " At some point, there will be NFL teams outside the USA ". If the Commissioner says it, then fans might as well accept that fate - though it will take many years for it come to fruition.

With the NFL International Series expanding mightily in recent years, this was always the inevitable step forward for the league. In 2026 , the league will host games in Australia, Brazil, France, Spain, Germany, Mexico, and England . The latter has become a staple of the International Series, as there has been a game played in London every year since 2007 (except the 2020 season, due to COVID).

London is considered the No. 1 city to host a new expansion NFL franchise

Given that the games in London have been such a success, that city is considered the top option for a potential expansion franchise . That notion has been heavily backed by former NFL quarterback Russell Wilson . The recently retired, iconic QB explained to Sky Sports why he believes that's the case.

In terms of a franchise coming out here playing NFL, the game has grown so much it's a worldwide game now. Taking it worldwide, London is probably the best place to do it, if you're going to go anywhere. The financial and media market here, the energy here around sports, and it's relatively easy to get to in terms of coming from America. It would be a great place to play, so I think that's a definite possibility for sure.

There have been rumors for several years that the NFL wanted the Jacksonville Jaguars to relocate to London. After all, they have played in London in 12-consecutive seasons when the league hosts games there .

But the Jaguars have no plans to leave Florida. The franchise revealed plans not too long ago for a renovation project at EverBank Stadium . Construction should be completed before the 2028 NFL season .

With the Jaguars no longer an option, the NFL will likely look into a fully new franchise that could set up shop in London. It just will take a while to get there.

articles.title: Pat McAfee’s scathing response to criticism of his debut album, which has been labelled ‘AI-generated rubbish’
articles.standfirst: The ESPN star insists the music is genuinely his work as listeners question the unusual country-rap project
articles.summary: The ESPN star insists the music is genuinely his work as listeners question the unusual country-rap project
articles.body:
Pat McAfee has never been someone who shies away from doing things his own way, but his latest venture has produced a reaction that even the outspoken sports media personality appears to find difficult.

The former NFL punter released his debut album, The Diary of a Polarizing Figure, on August 14. The 14-track project, which runs for roughly 42 minutes, blends country and rap influences and represents the culmination of songwriting McAfee says he has been doing for around two decades.

Instead of receiving universal support, however, the album has become the subject of widespread online mockery. Some listeners have questioned whether artificial intelligence was involved in creating the record, with particularly harsh critics dismissing it as “AI slop” or “AI-generated rubbish.”

McAfee addressed the backlash directly during a recent question-and-answer session on Instagram, admitting that the response has been difficult but insisting that the project is deeply personal.

“It sucks,” McAfee wrote on his Instagram Story. “I don’t love it.. being a “polarizing figure” isn’t fun, I’d like to be liked by everybody but it’s just not my reality.. never has been BUT, everything always sounds like an echo.

"Folks trying to impress each other. I understand folks hate me but I also know folks are definitely gonna let their jokes fly about me.. Charge it to the game.

“I like the songs a lot. I’m very proud of them. I wrote and sang every word for a 14 song album. The people who put the music around the words are legitimately some of the most talented musicians to ever exist...

"So I just think 5-10-20 years from now when my kids are listening to the songs they’ll know who their dad is... and for that, I’m pumped. Cheers man, thanks for the love.”

Project was about more than music

The controversy over artificial intelligence appears to have become one of the defining talking points surrounding the album. McAfee has pushed back against the suggestion that the record was simply generated by technology, while Nashville singer-songwriter Ernest has also spoken about the process behind the project.

Ernest , who collaborated with McAfee , has said that McAfee used an AI music generator to help create some early demos before the songs were developed in the studio.

That detail has apparently contributed to speculation from some listeners that AI was responsible for far more of the finished product.

Ernest , however, has defended the effort McAfee put into writing the material: “He’s not a musician, but he’s definitely a fan of music and he’s been writing lyrics for years. His phone is so full of notes.”

The album's production involved musicians in Nashville, with McAfee previously explaining that the project was brought to life with help from Ernest and other experienced music professionals. His interest in songwriting isn't entirely new, either. Before the album, he released the single “Dookie” in 2025.

There has certainly been no shortage of criticism. Some reviews have been particularly severe, while others have treated the album as an entertaining extension of McAfee's deliberately unconventional personality.

At least one ESPN colleague, Dan Orlovsky , publicly praised the record, calling it “legit good good,” illustrating just how divided the reaction has been.

For McAfee , though, the response appears to matter less than the personal reason for making the album.

“I’ve been writing songs about it all for 20yrs. It’s time to let them aht..,” McAfee wrote previously. “There’s A LOT of headlines & narratives about me.. if I was to die, I’d like my kids to know exactly who and what their dad is.”

That motivation puts the album in a different context. Rather than simply trying to establish himself as a recording artist, McAfee has described the project as a personal record of his experiences, frustrations and life in the public eye.

That public life has consistently attracted strong reactions. McAfee built his profile after retiring from professional football in 2017, transforming himself from an Indianapolis Colts punter into one of the most prominent figures in sports media.

His success with The Pat McAfee Show eventually led to a major relationship with ESPN, while his work on College GameDay has made him a familiar face to an even wider audience.

The album therefore fits a familiar pattern for McAfee which is to take a risk, embrace the criticism and continue regardless.

Whether listeners ultimately consider The Diary of a Polarizing Figure a serious musical project, an eccentric experiment or something else entirely, McAfee has already achieved one thing the title promised. People are talking about it.

And for someone who has spent much of his career turning controversy and unconventional ideas into part of his appeal, that may be exactly where he is most comfortable.

articles.title: Dolphins and Giants’ ‘rules of engagement’ don't last long as late hit sparks all-out brawl
articles.standfirst: It looked over for a moment, then everything exploded again
articles.summary: It looked over for a moment, then everything exploded again
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins and New York Giants arrived at Thursday’s joint practice with something that sounded almost improbable, almost diplomatic: “rules of engagement.” Coaches Jeff Hafley and John Harbaugh had agreed on limits designed to keep things physical while ensuring safety, protecting the quarterbacks and avoiding unnecessary hits. It seemed like a good plan, a good initiative with very good intentions, but in the end, it was simply wishful thinking.

Tensions erupted during Thursday’s session in Miami Gardens, ahead of the preseason game the two teams will play this Saturday, August 22. The fight broke out after a late hit on Giants wide receiver Calvin Austin III. Players rushed toward the sideline, shoving began and, within seconds, Dolphins and Giants jerseys disappeared into a massive tangle of bodies. Even Jameis Winston got caught up in the chaos, while Giants personnel tried to keep quarterback Jaxson Dart away from the pile so he wouldn’t get physically involved.

When you disguise intent as a late hit

The strangest thing about the video is how quickly everything changes. For a moment, it looks like the players have managed to separate those involved in the initial confrontation. Some are clearly trying to pull their teammates away, others simply arrive to see what happened, and neither side seems particularly interested in escalating the situation.

Then someone refuses to let it go. Tempers flare again and suddenly the group becomes even bigger. What appeared to be over just seconds earlier erupts all over again.

And that wasn’t the only confrontation of the day. Reports from the joint practice described several altercations, including punches being thrown at different points. One Dolphins player was ejected from practice after throwing a punch, while another earlier confrontation reportedly involved Giants linebacker Abdul Carter.

A morning of joint practice intended to improve strategies and evaluate players between Miami and New York only made Saturday’s preseason game much more interesting. The repeated back-and-forth provocation showed just how little these two teams seemed to tolerate each other Thursday , and now they’ll have to prove who is better on the field, not in the ring.

There is no historic Dolphins-Giants rivalry behind all of this. They rarely even meet during the regular season. Their most recent regular-season matchup came on October 8, 2023, when Miami defeated New York 31-16 at Hard Rock Stadium.

The Dolphins piled up more than 500 yards that afternoon, while Giants quarterback Daniel Jones was sacked six times and eventually left the game with a neck injury. In fact, Miami has won the last two regular-season meetings between the teams, including a 20-9 victory in 2021.

The absence of a traditional rivalry might make what happened Thursday even more interesting. These aren’t division rivals carrying years of bad blood. They were two teams that, in theory, were supposed to help each other prepare for the season , and yet they couldn’t make it through a single joint practice without tempers repeatedly boiling over.

Now they’ll see each other again almost immediately. The Giants return to Hard Rock Stadium to face the Dolphins in Week 2 of the NFL preseason on Saturday, August 22.

Preseason games usually create more questions about roster spots than personal grudges. But after what happened Thursday, every hard tackle, every late shove and every extra word after the whistle will suddenly carry a different meaning.

The coaches wanted to establish “rules of engagement.” Their players may have just given an otherwise routine preseason game something far more valuable: a reason to watch.

articles.title: The wild trend of NFL rookies begging to be cut after court ruling causes chaos throughout league
articles.standfirst: Battle over NCAA eligibility has created an unprecedented dilemma for players fighting to make NFL rosters
articles.summary: Battle over NCAA eligibility has created an unprecedented dilemma for players fighting to make NFL rosters
articles.body:
NFL roster cuts normally represent something players spend an entire summer trying to avoid. This preseason, however, several rookies reportedly have a very different request for their teams to release them now.

A series of court decisions challenging NCAA eligibility rules has created a potential route back to college football for certain players from the high school Class of 2022, including some who have already signed NFL contracts.

With the legal battle moving quickly, players on the fringes of NFL rosters now have another option to consider before the season begins. Former NFL executive Andrew Brandt highlighted just how unusual the situation has become.

“Now hearing of a few players going to their NFL teams and asking to be cut now (instead of likely being cut in two weeks) to go play in college again,” Brandt wrote on X. “What a time this is.”

The uncertainty stems from legal challenges arguing that affected athletes should receive another season of college eligibility. A Louisiana court added another layer Wednesday by granting a temporary restraining order involving 33 athletes, including 16 football players.

Some of those players are already much further along than simply preparing for another college season.

NFL contracts suddenly aren't only option

Tampa Bay Buccaneers linebacker Jack Pyburn , Cleveland Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright , Seattle Seahawks running back Anthony Hankerson and Arizona Cardinals defensive back Wydett Williams are among the notable players caught up in the eligibility situation.

The possibility of returning isn't merely theoretical. Wright, TJ Harden, Zxavian Harris and Weylin Lapuaho have reportedly already entered the transfer portal.

Perhaps the most striking cases involve Pyburn and Williams , who have already appeared in NFL preseason games. Pyburn recorded two sacks for the Buccaneers , yet another college season could now potentially be available if the legal process ultimately goes his way.

The Browns , meanwhile, have been evaluating depth at tight end while Wright has been absent from training camp, according to The Athletic's Zac Jackson.

There are financial considerations as well. Wright, Williams and Pyburn reportedly received signing bonuses below $25,000, while guaranteed salary provisions could further complicate what happens if they are released.

Court decision could create 'chaos'

The NCAA has strongly opposed the legal challenges and warned of broader consequences if additional eligibility is granted.

Senior vice president Tim Buckley said the ruling “invites further chaos in college sports and irreparably harms thousands of student-athletes already on campus.”

That leaves the players caught between an immediate NFL opportunity and the possibility of returning to college, potentially improving their draft stock and pursuing another season in a rapidly changing college football landscape.

Time is also becoming a factor. NFL clubs must reduce their rosters to 53 players by August 30, meaning decisions surrounding those on the roster bubble are approaching quickly.

Players have spent generations treating an NFL contract as the final destination after college. This eligibility dispute has produced the remarkable possibility that, for a handful of rookies, getting released might suddenly be the opportunity they're hoping to receive.

articles.title: Arch Manning drops a beautiful deep ball that shows exactly why NFL scouts are watching
articles.summary: Arch Manning only needed one throw to show one of the qualities that could make him such an intriguing NFL prospect.
articles.body:
Arch Manning only needed one throw to show one of the qualities that could make him such an intriguing NFL prospect.

The Texas quarterback launched a gorgeous deep ball downfield, putting just the right amount of touch underneath it and dropping it into his receiver’s hands in stride. The placement is what makes the play stand out: the receiver barely has to adjust.

That ability is becoming an important part of the conversation surrounding Manning. One NFL scout reportedly identified his deep ball as “one of his best” traits, and throws like this make it easy to understand why evaluators are paying attention.

The Manning name guarantees expectations will always be enormous, but ultimately Arch has to create his own résumé. Arm talent, touch and throws like this are the kind of evidence that matters and the kind of plays that can make an NFL team start imagining what he could eventually become.

articles.title: "One in four" would not be the whole story: the chilling finding shaking the NFL
articles.standfirst: A study changed the conversation about hits in the NFL: Of the 878 former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021, 235 donated their brains and 215 showed signs of CTE
articles.summary: A study changed the conversation about hits in the NFL: Of the 878 former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021, 235 donated their brains and 215 showed signs of CTE
articles.body:
The NFL is once again under scrutiny because of the long-term consequences that repeated blows to the head can have. A study published this Tuesday found signs of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) in 215 of the 235 brains of former players that were donated for research.

This means that in 91.4% of the brains examined, records of brain damage caused by repeated trauma were found.

The figure that explains why the study is different

"C TE is a neurodegenerative disease associated with repeated impacts to the head. One of the aspects that most concerns specialists is that it can remain unconfirmed during a person's lifetime, since the definitive diagnosis can only be made after death.

In this case, the novelty of the work lies in the fact that it was not limited to analyzing only those who donated their brains.

The research was based on 878 former players who died between 2016 and 2021, of whom 235 donated their brains for the research, and from this it emerged that 215 showed signs of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE).

If the 215 confirmed cases were the only ones among the 878 former players, the prevalence would be 24.5%. In other words, at least one in four had died with the disease.

The study also found that the progression of the disease was related to cognitive problems. Among donors with CTE, 61.3% met the clinical criteria for dementia , and the most severe forms showed an even stronger association with that decline.

Another aspect highlighted by the work is that the hits associated with the disease can accumulate over many years. Part of that exposure occurs before players reach the NFL, even during youth and college stages.

The analysis of death certificates provided another important element. Among former players whose brains were not donated, researchers found 215 cases in which a neurodegenerative disease appeared as the cause of death. Although this data does not allow confirming that those people suffered from CTE, it does represent an indication that could point to a higher prevalence than initially estimated.

A disease that can appear years later

"CTE is related to repeated blows to the head over time. It is not an injury that is necessarily noticeable right away: its effects can appear years later and be associated with memory problems, behavioral changes, and cognitive difficulties.

In addition, there is a particularity that makes the picture even more complicated. The disease cannot be confirmed with certainty while the person is alive. To detect it, it is necessary to study the brain after death, so it is still difficult to know how many former players may have developed it.

articles.title: NFL set new discipline rules: Three violations in one season now bring a one-game suspension
articles.standfirst: Though violations will carry over into future seasons, all players will begin 2026 with a clean slate
articles.summary: Though violations will carry over into future seasons, all players will begin 2026 with a clean slate
articles.body:
Each season, the NFL approves new regulations that team owners and the NFLPA meticulously negotiate during the offseason, primarily prioritizing the safety of the players who serve as the heartbeat of the world's most competitive league.

From outlawing helmet-to-helmet collisions and horse-collar tackles years ago to introducing restrictions on hip-drop tackles and completely overhauling the kickoff rules last season, the game constantly evolves to protect its athletes while fostering an increasingly explosive, high-scoring brand of football that fans demand.

NFL and NFLPA New Three-Strike Suspension Rule

In a joint announcement ahead of the upcoming campaign, the league and the players' association unveiled a revamped on-field discipline framework following months of collaborative planning.

Briefed to club executives during league meetings in Atlanta and formally approved by player leadership at a Board of Player Representatives meeting, the updated policy targets five specific health and safety infractions proven to carry the highest risk of severe injury:

Hits on defenseless players

Under the new protocol, any player who commits three violations across these categories during a single season will face an automatic one-game suspension .

To ensure a fair transition, every player enters the 2026 season with a completely clean slate, though accumulated infractions will carry forward into future years while offering a streamlined appeal process.

Shared Accountability: Fines, Rebates, and Mandatory Coach Meetings

The updated disciplinary system introduces unique incentives and accountability measures for both athletes and coaching staffs . Players who commit only a single violation throughout the entire year will now receive 50 percent of their fine refunded at the season's conclusion, rewarding isolated mistakes over chronic offender habits.

However, players approaching the dangerous three-strike suspension threshold will be mandated to attend formal review meetings alongside their head coaches and league officials.

Furthermore, organizations plagued by excessive health and safety penalties will face steeper financial sanctions, while former players and coaches, including veteran defender and former head coach Ron Rivera , will join the pool of independent officers overseeing player appeal hearings.

articles.title: NFL retires the Pro Bowl starting this season while keeping Pro Bowl selections and honors
articles.standfirst: The selection process for the Pro Bowl will remain the same, with a total of 88 players from both conferences being honored
articles.summary: The selection process for the Pro Bowl will remain the same, with a total of 88 players from both conferences being honored
articles.body:
For top sports leagues like Major League Baseball and the NBA , as well as the NFL with its traditional Pro Bowl , finding a format that consistently captures fan interest and strong television ratings in recent years has proven remarkably difficult.

While the NBA has continually tweaked its mid-season showcase, gravitating toward a competitive Team USA versus Team World format, the NFL has finally decided to pull the plug on its exhibition game.

Dating back to 1951 , the Pro Bowl will officially be retired starting this season , with league executives and team owners acknowledging that the primary culprit behind its demise was a severe, ongoing lack of on-field competitiveness.

From traditional NFC versus AFC matchups to conference-agnostic rosters and, most recently, a non-contact flag football experiment, the league explored every avenue before concluding that a standalone all-star game is no longer viable.

Transforming the Pro Bowl Into an Elite Individual Honor Without the Game

Following years of player surveys and declining engagement, the NFL is pivoting by turning the Pro Bowl into a pure individual accolade rather than a physical game. A total of 88 players will receive official Pro Bowl honors each year , entirely eliminating the chaotic cascade of alternate selections that bloated rosters out of proportion in recent seasons.

Peter O'Reilly , the NFL's executive vice president of club business, international, and league events, candidly explained to The Athletic that all-star games across major sports have struggled for a long time to genuinely showcase the elite premium of athletic competition.

In lieu of the actual game or skills competitions, the selected Pro Bowlers will gather in Los Angeles for a high-profile, in-person celebration every February.

The selection process itself remains unchanged, utilizing ballots cast equally by fans, players, and coaches to determine the final 88 standouts across offense, defense, and special teams from both conferences.

Financial Implications, Incentives, and the Road to the 2028 Olympics

Without a live game to play, maintaining the rigorous process of naming Pro Bowlers might seem redundant, but financial stakes and contractual incentives keep the system vital.

Countless player contracts contain lucrative financial incentives tied directly to Pro Bowl nods.

Furthermore, rookie contracts for non-first-round draft picks feature performance escalators, while the valuable fifth-year option for first-round selections can scale significantly higher depending on how many Pro Bowl appearances a player accumulates.

To encourage participation in the new Los Angeles gathering, the league has built-in unique motivation: Los Angeles will host the 2028 Summer Olympics , where flag football will make its historic Olympic debut.

The NFL plans major promotional activations leading up to the global games, creating a natural bridge where the world's best football players can gather at the future Olympic site, building excitement for flag football's international showcase.

articles.title: Career in danger? Miles Sanders found slumped over wheel in shocking DUI arrest
articles.standfirst: The veteran NFL running back is currently a free agent with the 2026 season approaching.
articles.summary: The veteran NFL running back is currently a free agent with the 2026 season approaching.
articles.body:
Miles Sanders is facing fresh uncertainty over his NFL future after details emerged of a DUI arrest in Pennsylvania earlier this summer.

The 29-year-old running back, who remains unsigned ahead of the 2026 regular season, was arrested on June 8 in Churchill Borough, near Pittsburgh.

Court records reportedly show Sanders was charged last week with driving under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance, along with careless driving.

The timing could prove particularly damaging for Sanders , who is attempting to find another NFL opportunity after spending the 2025 season with the Dallas Cowboys .

Police reportedly found Sanders slumped behind wheel

According to police, Sanders was discovered inside a vehicle that had stopped in the middle of the road.

Officers reportedly described the former Philadelphia Eagles player as being "in and out of consciousness" while slumped in the driver's seat.

Police further alleged that Sanders smelled strongly of alcohol and performed poorly during a field sobriety test.

Authorities claim Sanders acknowledged consuming alcohol earlier in the day before a breath test produced a positive result. Police also said marijuana was discovered inside the vehicle.

Sanders has not publicly addressed the allegations himself.

His attorney Phil DiLucente told CBS Pittsburgh: "This is a private matter that has not even reached the preliminary hearing stage and there will be no further comment."

Miles Sanders already fighting for NFL future

The arrest comes at a delicate point in Sanders ' career, with the running back currently without a team and the new NFL season only weeks away.

Sanders entered the league when the Eagles selected him in the second round of the 2019 NFL Draft after his college career at Penn State.

He spent four seasons in Philadelphia before joining the Carolina Panthers , where he played for two years. Sanders then moved to Dallas for the 2025 campaign.

Now a free agent at 29, any off-field concerns could potentially complicate his efforts to secure another contract as teams finalize their rosters.

The legal process is also still at an early stage, meaning the allegations against Sanders haven't yet been tested at a preliminary hearing.

Sanders is scheduled to return to court on October 28 for that hearing.

articles.standfirst: The trade deadline this season is November 10, which gives teams until Week 9 to make changes
articles.summary: The trade deadline this season is November 10, which gives teams until Week 9 to make changes
articles.body:
With the final NFL preseason games happening this Saturday, teams are ready to begin the season with the illusion of reaching Super Bowl 61 at SoFi Stadium on February 14, 2027 .

After training camps and the preseason, clubs must now know who their 11 starters are on offense and defense, except for the Atlanta Falcons , who are still sorting out their competition between quarterbacks Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr.

But as we know, seasons rarely unfold exactly as anticipated, which is why midseason trades frequently occur to bolster a roster exceeding expectations or to hoard draft picks if a campaign goes sideways and teams pivot toward the future.

A clear example from recent years involves the New York Jets , who pulled the plug on a struggling campaign by trading two top defensive stars in Quinnen Williams (to the Cowboys) and Sauce Gardner (to the Colts), players who now anchor their new squads.

Notable Names Surface in Trade Rumors Before Deadline

The conclusion of the preseason means the annual NFL roster cutdown day is fast approaching. By 6:00 p.m. ET this Sunday night, all 32 franchises must slash their rosters from 90 down to 53 players for the 2026 season, leaving over 1,000 players to be released , waived, or shelved with injury designations.

Some, however, will find new life via trade, much like this week's swap between the Patriots and Texans sending wideout Kayshon Boutte to Houston after losing Jayden Higgins for the year to a torn ACL.

Three prominent names stand out as prime candidates to be moved before the upcoming deadline:

Anthony Richardson ( Indianapolis Colts , QB ): Drafted No. 4 overall in 2023 , Richardson has struggled to find consistent footing, starting just 15 games across three seasons while battling various injuries, including the bizarre orbital fracture that wiped out his 2025 campaign, and benchings due to poor execution. He holds an 8–7 record as a starter, accumulating 21 total touchdowns against 17 turnovers . Though the Colts granted him permission to seek a trade earlier in the offseason, he remains in Indianapolis as Sunday's deadline looms.

J.J. McCarthy ( Minnesota Vikings, QB ): With veteran Kyler Murray securing Minnesota's starting job, the 2024 first-round pick is ostensibly slated as the backup, though recent practice reports complicate that narrative. McCarthy split reps with veteran Carson Wentz as the primary backup earlier in the week before sitting out with an ankle injury sustained against the Ravens. This fluid situation could either solidify the 23-year-old's spot or prompt inquiring phone calls from external front offices.

Kayvon Thibodeaux ( New York Giants, Edge ): Head coach John Harbaugh addressed trade chatter surrounding Thibodeaux this spring, noting that while everyone is technically movable, the 25-year-old edge rusher is a talented player in peak physical condition. Caught in a crowded pass-rushing room alongside Brian Burns and Abdul Carter , Thibodeaux, the No. 5 pick in the 2022 draft , is entering the final year of his rookie deal with a $14.7 million fifth-year option attached. Having racked up 23.5 sacks and six forced fumbles in his career, he represents an enticing piece for any contender looking to shore up its pass rush before September kicks off.

articles.title: Tony Romo's CBS future hangs in the balance after three new citations from his DUI arrest
articles.standfirst: Romo was arrested in July on suspicion of driving under the influence, and there is still no set date for his return to CBS
articles.summary: Romo was arrested in July on suspicion of driving under the influence, and there is still no set date for his return to CBS
articles.body:
Following his arrest on July 23 in Wisconsin, former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo finds his high-profile broadcasting career on indefinite pause just weeks before the kickoff of the regular season.

The 46-year-old analyst, who accumulated 34,183 passing yards and 248 touchdowns during his 14-year NFL career, was placed on administrative leave by network executives on July 31. While Romo is on leave, he has been replaced on CBS' top broadcasting team by former NFL superstar JJ. Watt , who will now team up with the legendary play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz and sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson .

Tony Romo Faces Legal Citations

The legal troubles surrounding the lead commentator intensified on Thursday evening when court filings confirmed three formal citations stemming from the traffic stop .

Local authorities cited Romo with a first-offense operating while intoxicated (OWI) , an illegal passing maneuver on the right side of the roadway, and carrying open intoxicants inside his vehicle .

With an official court hearing set for September 21, the legal procedure guarantees that Romo will remain out of the booth through at least the first three weeks of the campaign.

Addressing the latest developments, a representative for Romo released a statement emphasizing accountability: " Tony accepts full responsibility for his actions and has taken proactive steps to ensure that this isolated civil matter is properly resolved. We are working with local authorities to bring this matter to a close, and we are communicating with CBS about next steps."

Despite that outreach, CBS Sports President David Berson publicly affirmed that the network has established no timetable for his potential return, keeping the analyst sidelined indefinitely while leadership monitors the proceedings.

This extended absence has led numerous sports media insiders to suggest that Romo may never reclaim his position on CBS's primary broadcast team .

The stakes are immense, given the historic contract Romo inked back in 2020, a 10-year, $180 million agreement that still holds $72 million in remaining compensation.

With network executives evaluating their long-term options and Watt stepping into the spotlight alongside Nantz, Romo's once-unshakable standing as the crown jewel of NFL color commentary hangs in serious jeopardy.

articles.title: NFL honors BTS members with personalized footballs featuring their names and Chicago concert dates
articles.standfirst: The unusual souvenirs feature each member’s name and the dates of the Soldier Field shows
articles.summary: The unusual souvenirs feature each member’s name and the dates of the Soldier Field shows
articles.body:
BTS ’ time in Chicago may already be over, but the group’s two-night visit to Soldier Field will see them head home with items they won’t soon forget.

Following their long-awaited return to the city, all seven members were reportedly seen with personalized NFL -style footballs featuring their names and the dates of their Chicago concerts.

The unusual souvenirs surfaced online after the members attended soundcheck ahead of their second show on August 28.

Photos shared by fans appear to show individual footballs customized for each member, transforming a distinctly American sports item into a memento tied directly to BTS’ ARIRANG World Tour.

The red-and-white footballs feature “BTS: WORLD TOUR” across the white section, while “AUGUST 27 & 28, 2026” appears underneath. Each football also has one member’s name printed on it.

While fans have speculated about the exact origin of the items, the photographs offer a clear look at the personalized designs.

One image shows a member holding a football inside the stadium, while another gives fans a closer view of the lettering and concert dates.

A special keepsake from BTS’ Chicago return

The personalized footballs arrived during an especially important moment for BTS and their fans. The group performed at Soldier Field on August 27 and 28, marking their first Chicago concerts in seven years.

The return was highly anticipated after the group’s lengthy break from touring together.

More than 60,000 members of ARMY gathered at Soldier Field for the opening concert, with fans traveling from different parts of the United States to attend. The weekend also featured BTS-themed meetups, merchandise lines and other fan activities across Chicago.

The concerts represented the chance for many fans to finally see all seven members together onstage again after the COVID-19 pandemic interrupted the group’s planned 2020 world tour.

BTS’ subsequent hiatus also included the members’ staggered mandatory military service in South Korea.

The enthusiasm surrounding the Chicago shows showed the deep connection between BTS and ARMY. Fans have often credited the group’s music and message with helping them through difficult periods, while BTS has built a reputation for addressing themes including self-acceptance, mental health and personal growth.

Chicago itself embraced the occasion, with Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker declaring August 27 and 28 “BTS Days” in recognition of the group’s global influence and their performances at Soldier Field.

With that in mind, the customized footballs have become an especially fitting souvenir, combining BTS’ Chicago experience with a famous piece of American sports culture, while the individual names make each item personal to a member.

articles.title: Instant reaction: Shilo Sanders promotes his new album with the wild fight that cost him his NFL career
articles.standfirst: The former Colorado star is embracing the controversy that followed him out of the NFL
articles.summary: The former Colorado star is embracing the controversy that followed him out of the NFL
articles.body:
Shilo Sanders has found an unusual way to revisit one of the most controversial moments of his short-lived NFL career. The former Colorado safety released his latest music album, World of Headache, on Sunday, and its rollout has already generated plenty of discussion among football fans.

The album appears to draw heavily from Sanders ’ brief professional football experience, particularly the incident that brought his time with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to an abrupt end.

Sanders entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2025 after going unselected during the draft. The Buccaneers gave him an opportunity to compete for a place on their roster, but his preseason campaign ended after an altercation with Buffalo Bills tight end Zach Davidson.

During a preseason matchup, tensions between Sanders and Davidson escalated before the former Colorado player threw a punch. The incident resulted in Sanders being ejected, and Tampa Bay subsequently waived him ahead of the regular-season roster deadline. The NFL also handed Sanders a $4,669 fine for the incident.

While the altercation became a defining moment of Sanders ’ NFL journey, he now appears to be embracing it rather than attempting to distance himself from it.

Shilo Sanders brings his NFL controversy into the music world

The title of his new album, World of Headache, already hints at a project built around personal struggles and difficult experiences. That connection becomes even more obvious with the album’s opening track, Go Out Swinging.

The song title appears to reference the punch that ended Sanders ’ time in Tampa Bay, but the album artwork has attracted even more attention. The cover uses imagery inspired by the infamous preseason confrontation, although there’s a significant change to the original scene.

Instead of Davidson , the artwork depicts Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid as the player involved in the confrontation. Kincaid wasn’t the player Sanders fought during the preseason game, and that detail quickly became a talking point among fans.

Social media reactions were largely critical. Some fans accused Sanders of attempting to generate publicity by altering the incident, while others questioned why he would continue drawing attention to an episode that contributed to the end of his NFL opportunity.

The decision to feature Kincaid also left some observers wondering whether the artwork was intended purely as a provocative marketing move.

Not everyone in the Sanders family seemed bothered by the controversy, however. Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders, Shilo’s younger brother, reacted to the album post with a simple but supportive comment: “Legendary.”

Shilo’s football future now appears uncertain after he hinted earlier this year that he could be moving on from the sport. Music may therefore represent a new direction for the Sanders brother, giving him an opportunity to build an identity beyond football.

articles.title: Which notable NFL players were among the biggest surprises of the 2026 roster cuts?
articles.standfirst: Even if their teams have cut them, these players can still sign with another team now or during the season
articles.summary: Even if their teams have cut them, these players can still sign with another team now or during the season
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL preseason is over and now we are just days away from the season opener in a Super Bowl rematch between the Seattle Seahawks and the New England Patriots that this year will take place on a Wednesday instead of the traditional Thursday.

The reason for the shift is that Thursday features the first regular-season game in NFL history hosted in Australia , and due to the significant time zone difference, although the matchup kicks off locally on Friday, it lands on Thursday night back in the United States.

Surprise NFL Roster Cuts for the 2026 Season

Over the weekend, all 32 franchises finalized their initial 53-player rosters for the regular season, trimming down from the summer limit of 90 players. This massive contraction meant over 1,000 players were released , waived, or given injury designations, forcing veterans and former draft picks to look for work elsewhere.

While a fraction of these players will bounce back onto practice squads, many face an uncertain future. Several high-profile names caught analysts off guard by landing on the unemployment line:

Will Levis (QB): Selected 33rd overall in the 2023 draft , Levis started 21 games compiling a 5-16 record . After missing the entire 2025 season due to a shoulder injury, the Titans parted ways with the quarterback, who finishes his tenure in Tennessee with 3,899 passing yards, 21 touchdowns, 16 interceptions , and an 82.7 passer rating.

Evan Neal (OL): Drafted 7th overall in 2022 , Neal started 27 games exclusively at right tackle. Having missed the entire 2025 campaign due to injury , his sudden release stands out as one of the most shocking roster moves given his elite draft pedigree.

Jaydon Blue (RB): A fifth-round selection for the Cowboys in 2025, Blue finishes his initial stint having appeared in 5 games with 38 carries for 129 yards (a 3.4 average) and 1 touchdown , alongside 1 reception for 5 yards and 3 kick returns for 72 yards.

Dameon Pierce (RB): A fourth-round pick for Houston in 2022 who spent time with the Chiefs, Pierce has accumulated 419 rushes for 1,684 yards (4.0 average) and 8 touchdowns across 43 career games. He has since re-anchored himself onto the Eagles' practice squad.

Mecole Hardman (WR): Taken 56th overall in 2019 , the three-time Super Bowl champion with the Chiefs has experienced a difficult time finding stable footing outside of Kansas City. Across 82 career games, he has recorded 178 receptions for 2,302 yards (12.9 average) and 16 touchdowns , alongside his 2019 Pro Bowl nod as a return specialist.

Marquez Valdes-Scantling (WR): A veteran former fifth-round pick of the Packers who has since suited up for the Chiefs (winning 2 Super Bowls), Bills, Saints, 49ers, and Steelers, Valdes-Scantling was most recently cut by the Cowboys. Across 116 career appearances, he has hauled in 219 receptions for 3,686 yards (16.8 average) and 21 touchdowns .

articles.title: Kylie Beck surprises fans by revealing her dream involving her brother Carson as they both enter the NFL
articles.standfirst: The new Miami Dolphins cheerleader is living through a special moment as her brother also prepares to begin his professional journey.
articles.summary: The new Miami Dolphins cheerleader is living through a special moment as her brother also prepares to begin his professional journey.
articles.body:
Kylie Beck is experiencing a moment she will likely remember for a long time . After becoming one of the newest cheerleaders for the Miami Dolphins , the young woman is preparing for her official debut with the franchise while enjoying a completely different chapter in her life.

The season is about to begin, and with it will come a very special coincidence for her family.

A new uniform and a new beginning

Kylie announced in June that she had joined the Miami cheerleading team, an opportunity that comes after several years of building her own presence on social media, where she regularly shares content related to fashion, beauty, dance and lifestyle.

Now, her routine will also be connected to Dolphins game days. Her official debut is scheduled for Sunday, September 13, when Miami visits the Las Vegas Raiders .

But that day will carry an even greater meaning for her family.

Carson Beck is also ready to make the jump

The quarterback was selected by the Arizona Cardinals with the 65th overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , in the third round, and later signed a four-year contract with the franchise.

After playing in his first preseason game with Arizona on August 6, Carson is now preparing for his regular-season debut against the Los Angeles Chargers, also on September 13 .

The coincidence is certainly an unusual one: while Kylie will be on the sidelines in Miami, Carson will be on the field with Arizona.

Their paths have yet to cross

There is, however, one thing keeping their stories apart for now.

The Dolphins and Cardinals are not scheduled to play each other during the 2026 regular season . That means that, for the siblings to meet in an official game, a much more complicated possibility would have to emerge: both teams would need to reach the playoffs and eventually face one another.

And that was precisely the possibility that sparked Kylie's imagination.

The question that took her all the way to the Super Bowl

During an appearance on The 305Club podcast , Kylie talked about what it would mean to see Miami face Arizona.

Her response revealed just how much she loves the idea. She acknowledged that it would be an exciting moment and said she would love for their respective teams to meet someday .

Then she took the conversation one step further.

“One day, the Super Bowl. Let's manifest that right.”

The comment completely changed the tone of the conversation. Kylie was not talking about an immediate possibility or claiming that it would happen; she was simply putting forward the scenario that, for her, would be the most special of all.

And it is easy to understand why she would dream about it that way: not every day do two siblings begin their NFL journeys at almost the same time, from two very different places within the league .

articles.title: Inside Nashville’s $2.1 Billion Nissan Stadium Set to Host Super Bowl 2030
articles.standfirst: The Tennessee Titans are building one of the NFL’s most ambitious new venues — and Nashville is already preparing for its biggest sporting event ever.
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans are building one of the NFL’s most ambitious new venues — and Nashville is already preparing for its biggest sporting event ever.
articles.body:
N ASHVILLE — A new era is taking shape on the banks of the Cumberland River.

The Tennessee Titans’ new Nissan Stadium , a $2.1 billion project, is under construction and scheduled to open in 2027. Just three years later, the venue will welcome Super Bowl LXIV , bringing the NFL’s biggest game to Nashville for the first time.

The project is much more than a new home for the Titans. It is designed to become a year-round destination for football, concerts, major sporting events and entertainment.

With a capacity of approximately 60,000 fans, Nissan Stadium will feature a translucent roof, allowing events to take place throughout the year while protecting spectators from Nashville’s weather.

And the experience inside will be dramatically different from the Titans’ current home.

Fans will sit approximately 38% closer to the field, creating a more intimate atmosphere for NFL games. The stadium will also include outdoor terraces, panoramic views of Nashville and more than 15 spaces designed for events and hospitality.

Nashville’s Super Bowl moment

The biggest test will come in 2030.

Super Bowl LXIV will make Nashville the center of the American sports world, giving the city its first opportunity to host the NFL championship game.

The choice is another recognition of Nashville’s rapid growth as a sports and entertainment destination.

The city already proved its ability to host major NFL events when the 2019 NFL Draft brought more than 200,000 people to downtown Nashville.

Now, the city is preparing for an event on an entirely different scale.

More than a football stadium

The new Nissan Stadium is part of Nashville’s massive East Bank redevelopment and is expected to become one of the city’s defining landmarks.

For the Titans, it will provide a modern home built specifically around the fan experience.

For Nashville, it represents an opportunity to compete for the biggest sporting and entertainment events in the world.

The stadium is expected to open in 2027.

Then, in 2030, Nashville will take center stage when Super Bowl LXIV arrives at Nissan Stadium.

articles.title: Tony Romo's blood alcohol level was nearly twice the legal limit during Wisconsin OWI arrest
articles.standfirst: Court records reportedly reveal a .15 BAC following the former Cowboys quarterback's July arrest.
articles.summary: Court records reportedly reveal a .15 BAC following the former Cowboys quarterback's July arrest.
articles.body:
Tony Romo's blood alcohol concentration was reportedly close to twice Wisconsin's legal limit when the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback was arrested for operating while intoxicated in July.

articles.title: Who are the NFL MVP favorites? Two former winners among the top favorites for 2026
articles.standfirst: Since 2007, only one MVP has not been won by a quarterback: Adrian Peterson in 2012
articles.summary: Since 2007, only one MVP has not been won by a quarterback: Adrian Peterson in 2012
articles.body:
By this time next week, the 2026 NFL season will have already begun with all 32 teams aiming to reach Super Bowl 61 on February 14 at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles.

Of course, every franchise shares that ultimate dream, but like every season, heavy favorites like the loaded Los Angeles Rams sit alongside rebuilding squads essentially positioning themselves for the 2027 NFL Draft , such as the Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals.

Naturally, history proves that anything can happen over the course of a gruelling 18-week campaign, take last year, for instance, when the Seahawks and Patriots clashed in the Super Bowl despite neither being pegged among the primary preseason oddsmakers' favorites. Now, those same two resilient rivals kick off the brand-new year in a high-stakes opening rematch .

Top MVP Contenders and Early Betting Odds for the 2026 Campaign

Last season, Matthew Stafford earned a thoroughly deserved MVP crown after leading the league in passing yards ( 4,707 ) and touchdowns ( 46 ) for the first time in his stellar career while guiding his team to the NFC Championship game.

Entering the upcoming year, the 38-year-old signal-caller sits sixth ( +1200 ) across major sportsbooks, with four other premier quarterbacks positioned ahead of him, including last year’s MVP runner-up, Drake Maye (+1100) , who climbs to fourth while working with upgraded offensive weapons in his third professional campaign.

Ahead of them, the top three MVP betting favorites feature an elite group of game-changers:

Josh Allen (+650) : The 2024 MVP has finished inside the top five of MVP voting for four consecutive seasons, keeping the Bills anchored by the league's longest active playoff streak ( 7 straight years ) while accounting for over 35 touchdowns in each of the last six years. Allen transitions into this season under a new head coach in Joe Brady , who served as the team's offensive coordinator over the previous two seasons, while also gaining explosive wide receiver DJ Moore as a primary passing target.

Lamar Jackson (+850) : The two-time MVP enters a new era under first-year head coach Jesse Minter , an early favorite for Coach of the Year, following a career spent entirely under John Harbaugh. A healthy Jackson remains an unstoppable force as the greatest dual-threat quarterback in football history, holding the all-time record for quarterback rushing yards (6,522) , the highest career passer rating for any passer with a minimum of 1,500 attempts (102.2), and the most career games with a perfect passer rating.

Joe Burrow (+900) : Burrow hits the field looking to bounce back after appearing in just eight games last year, facing mounting pressure to secure a playoff berth or risk changes on the sideline with head coach Zac Taylor. Having already captured Comeback Player of the Year honors twice, Burrow views CPOY as a viable safety net if the MVP eludes him. During his last fully healthy season, he looked every bit like an MVP frontrunner after throwing for a league-high 4,918 passing yards and 43 touchdowns .

Rounding out the top tier just behind them sits Justin Herbert (+1000), who now operates under the guidance of offensive mastermind Mike McDaniel , a coordinator uniquely equipped to squeeze every ounce of production out of the Chargers' franchise quarterback.

articles.title: Erin Andrews stuns NFL fans with new workout photo ahead of FOX return
articles.standfirst: The longtime sideline reporter is preparing for another demanding year with FOX’s top NFL team
articles.summary: The longtime sideline reporter is preparing for another demanding year with FOX’s top NFL team
articles.body:
Erin Andrews is heading into another demanding NFL season, and the veteran FOX reporter is drawing attention before she even gets back on the sideline.

The 48-year-old broadcaster appeared in a new workout campaign this week after joining fitness brand NOBULL, giving fans a glimpse of how she is preparing for the travel-heavy grind of another football season.

Andrews will once again be part of FOX’s lead NFL broadcast team alongside Kevin Burkhardt, Tom Brady and Tom Rinaldi , putting her on some of the network’s biggest games throughout the year.

NOBULL framed the partnership around the work ethic that has defined Andrews’ career.

“Erin Andrews has built a career on showing up, doing the work, and getting better every day,” the company said. “That’s NOBULL. And it’s why we’re excited to officially welcome her to our team.”

The campaign image quickly drew praise online.

“Such a perfect match. Erin Andrews embodies showing up, doing the work, and getting better every day,” one fan wrote. Another added: “She’s the very best! This ad is so perfect! Ready to see her on the field!”

One of NFL’s most recognizable broadcasters

The reaction comes as Andrews prepares for yet another season at the center of FOX’s coverage.

Her role has evolved considerably since the early days of her career, but she has remained a fixture on major national broadcasts while working some of the league’s highest-profile games. That schedule demands more than simply showing up on Sundays.

Sideline reporters regularly deal with travel, early production meetings, long hours at stadiums and unpredictable conditions, making Andrews ’ focus on fitness an obvious part of her preparation. Fans noticed the effort.

“Great job Erin. You are so amazingly beautiful. NoBull is legit,” one commenter wrote. Another called her “such a beast,” while others responded with messages of support as the start of the season approaches.

Andrews is also balancing her broadcasting career with life as a mother, making the new campaign another example of how she has continued to maintain a high-profile role in sports television well into her fourth decade in the industry.

One of the darkest moments of her career

The workout campaign arrived during an emotional week for Andrews , who also spoke in unusually candid detail about the 2009 stalking incident that became one of the most traumatic episodes of her life.

During an appearance on Call Her Daddy, Andrews recalled the moment she was told that secretly recorded footage of her inside a hotel room had been posted online.

“I called my mom and dad right away,” Andrews said. “I was screaming, crying because it was me and it was me naked in a hotel room walking around.

“I just said to my dad, ‘It’s over, my career is over. No one’s going to take me seriously ever again.’”

Instead, Andrews went on to remain one of the most prominent figures in NFL broadcasting.

Now, with another season approaching and a new fitness partnership in place, the veteran reporter still putting in the work before the cameras turn back on.

articles.title: The NFL Under Fire: Former players demand stronger measures as concerns about CTE escalate
articles.standfirst: New CTE research has renewed questions over whether former players are receiving enough care after years of physical punishment
articles.summary: New CTE research has renewed questions over whether former players are receiving enough care after years of physical punishment
articles.body:
Mark Collins doesn't regret playing football. He won two Super Bowls, spent more than a decade in the NFL and understood that every season came with physical risk. His concern now is what happens after players leave the field and begin living with the consequences.

The former New York Giants safety was one of several retired players who spoke to Sports Illustrated following renewed attention on chronic traumatic encephalopathy, or CTE, and the long-term health of former NFL players. Collins ’ frustration was aimed squarely at the league.

He argued that the NFL has the resources to provide much more substantial financial support to the comparatively small group of men who actually played in the league.

“They could do a f**king lot more,” Collins said. “This is a $3 trillion business. They could put in an annual quasi-salary of $200,000 to former players, stuff like that. They could do a lot of other things.”

Danger doesn't end when a career does

Collins hasn't been diagnosed with a neurological condition, but that hasn't stopped him from thinking about what could lie ahead. He cited former players such as Dave Duerson and Roger Craig while describing the unease that comes with knowing he belongs to the same group.

“You go, O.K., it’s got to a point where that could be me,” Collins said. “That could have been me. Or is that what I’m going toward?”

His comments came after research examining former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021. Of the 235 players whose brains were donated for examination, 215 showed evidence of CTE.

That finding has only intensified a debate that has followed the league for years. Former Denver Broncos wide receiver Mark Jackson said he suffered “at least four documented concussions” and believes his own chances of having CTE are extremely high.

“Yeah, I have CTE. It’s almost 100% positive that I do because I have the documented cases in Minnesota,” Jackson said. “I’m disappointed that the NFL hasn’t shelled out a quarter of a million or three hundred thousand to every player and called it a day.”

Former stars want stronger lifetime protection

Collins was far from alone in calling for more. Hall of Fame quarterback Warren Moon said former players should have access to lifetime health support, including regular medical screening.

“I think the benefits have improved, but they haven’t improved enough, especially on the health side of it,” Moon said. “I think we should have lifetime health care as well.”

Hall of Fame safety LeRoy Butler made a similar argument: “The money is not the issue,” Butler said. “They have the money.”

The NFL has made significant changes around concussion protocols, medical testing, player safety and compensation for qualifying former players. Collins ’ position, however, is that acknowledging football’s inherent danger shouldn't end the conversation.

“This is something we signed up for. We get it,” Collins said. “But a lot of guys put their bodies on the line and sometimes things happen, but the league has to see that as well and take care of those guys who played this game, who got them rich.”
